Variables

　TJS2 variables are specified using the var keyword. In TJS2, variables cannot be used without being declared.
　The format of the var keyword is as follows:

tvar variable_name;
tMultiple variable names can also be specified by separating them with a , (comma). If an initial value is required for a variable,

tvar variable_name = initial_value;
tYou can assign an initial value to the variable using this format.

Example:
    var variable=0;
    var var2=variable+2;
    var var3="this is var3.";
    var var1,var2,var3;
    var a=0,b=1,c=3;

tVariables do not need to have their types specified upon declaration. They take on the type of whatever value is assigned to them. In addition, types are automatically converted during calculations or based on context.

Variable Names

tAll valid identifiers can be used as variable names.

Example:
    var ampan;
    var 123a;  // NG because it starts with a number
    var function; // NG because function is a reserved word
    var function1; // OK because it contains a reserved word but is not the reserved word itself
    var 変数その一; // So-called full-width characters can also be used

Redeclaration of Variables

tDeclaring a variable with the same name two or more times does not result in an error. However, if an initial value is specified in subsequent declarations, that initial value is assigned to the variable. If no initial value is provided in subsequent declarations, it becomes void.

Example:
    var a=0;
    var a; // Second declaration (does not cause an error, and a becomes void)
    var a=-1; // Third declaration (does not cause an error, and -1 is assigned to a)

Variable Scope

tVariables declared within a section enclosed by { } (a block) become variables valid only within that block—that is, local variables.
tAlso, unlike C, there are no restrictions on the positions where variables can be declared.

Example:
    while(t--)
    {
        var ratio=t/all; // Declares variable 'ratio'
        setRatio(ratio);
    }

    // When control moves here, 'ratio' has been deleted

    var test; // Variables can also be declared here

tIn addition, if a variable with the same name as a variable outside the block is declared inside the block, only the newly declared variable can be accessed within that block.

Example:
    var ratio=0;
    if(flag)
    {
        var ratio; // Variable with the same name as the variable declared outside the block

        ratio=buf.position / buf.totalTime; // Only ratio inside the block can be accessed
        setRatio(ratio);
    }

    // When exiting the block, ratio inside the block is deleted, but ratio outside the block remains
    ratio=-1;

Note
tWhen a variable is declared with var outside all scopes (called global scope), that variable becomes a member of the global object.
